correctness.rationale: The forward residuals are exactly three Laplace moments of one positive constant-height interval. A nonzero difference of two such functions changes sign no more than twice; a three-exponential strict Chebyshev interpolation separator then contradicts equality of all measured moments. A two-rate ratio leaves a local continuum as pulse duration varies, proving sharpness. For rates 1:2:3, exact algebra gives R=u+v, S=u²+uv+v², discriminant (u-v)², domain constraints, and determinant −γ²Δ²uv(u−v)⁴. The actual standalone checker passed 540 assertions including 513 exact-rational examples and 24 nonharmonic numerical inversions; these are diagnostic and the infinite statement is proved in RESULT.md. Risk: strict one-interval/common-contrast hypotheses and noise instability; no independent mathematical audit.

originality.rationale: Checked close ecological isotope-clock primary articles already formulate a single switch with unknown contrast and a two-switch (including return) model with known stage equilibrium signatures; neither inspected statement identifies both return ages and an unknown intermediate contrast from the sharp minimum of three distinct tissues. General Prony literature covers piecewise-signal reconstruction and node collision, but no inspected theorem was found to state the exact specified arbitrary-rate three-tissue identification plus closed harmonic feasible-data inverse. This is a qualified contribution; broad moment-theory implications and inaccessible older work remain priority risks. A previously recorded four-harmonic-channel first-order-uptake theorem explicitly uses the same single-pulse moment formula and differentiates one-pulse from two-pulse models; that harmonic special case is NOT claimed to be novel. The new scope is arbitrary distinct positive rates with a sharp three-tissue minimum for the single-pulse-with-unknown-height assumption.
residual_risks: Generic T-system or generalized Prony theorems may imply the specialized arbitrary-rate injectivity without an explicit ecology application.

value.rationale: The exact minimal number of tissue clocks under an uncalibrated intermediate diet gives a meaningful monitoring-design boundary for temporary return-to-baseline feeding. The strict feasible-domain inversion (harmonic rates) and fourth-power degeneracy at coincident switch times show both exact recoverability and its boundary. The unknown contrast adds a genuinely necessary parameter to prior two-tissue known-contrast switching models. No claim of empirical field accuracy or of a general optimal survey design is made. An earlier harmonic single-pulse formula is acknowledged; the all-distinct-rates result supplies a non-harmonic experimental-design generalization.
